entity_types.name: Host
entity_types.description: A Proxmox node or physical server that runs guests, e.g. pve-01, node-02, 'host db01'. Proxmox nodes are Hosts, never Locations.

entity_types.name: Guest
entity_types.description: An LXC container, VM or Docker container, e.g. 'LXC 104', 'CT 210', 'VM 100'. Anything named LXC/CT/VM plus a number is a Guest, never a Location or Object.

entity_types.name: Service
entity_types.description: A software application or service running on a host or guest, e.g. Nextcloud, Grafana, Postgres, Home Assistant. ANY named application is a Service, never an Organization or Object.

entity_types.name: Workflow
entity_types.description: An automation workflow or scheduled job (n8n workflow, Semaphore job, cron)

entity_types.name: Network
entity_types.description: A VLAN, subnet, IP range, DNS domain or public hostname, e.g. docs.example.com, VLAN 20, 192.168.10.0/24. Domains and hostnames are Networks, never Locations.

entity_types.name: Storage
entity_types.description: A storage pool, NFS/SMB share, dataset or backup datastore

entity_types.name: Incident
entity_types.description: A failure, outage or malfunction affecting infrastructure

entity_types.name: Decision
entity_types.description: A design or architecture decision together with its rationale

entity_types.name: Procedure
entity_types.description: Standard operating procedures and sequential instructions

entity_types.name: Location
entity_types.description: A real-world physical place (a city, a house, a room, a rack). NEVER a server, node, guest or domain.

entity_types.name: Organization
entity_types.description: A real-world company, institution or formal group of people. NEVER a software service, host or guest.

entity_types.name: Document
entity_types.description: Information content in various forms (books, articles, reports, etc.)

entity_types.name: Person
entity_types.description: An individual human referenced in the content

entity_types.name: Topic
entity_types.description: Subject or knowledge domain (use as last resort, never for infrastructure).

entity_types.name: Object
entity_types.description: A physical item or device that is not a server or guest (use as last resort).

edge_types.name: RelatesTo
edge_types.description: LAST RESORT: only when two entities are clearly associated and NO other edge type fits. Never use it when the text says where something runs, what it depends on, what it monitors or exposes.

edge_types.name: Requires
edge_types.description: A dependency: the source needs the target in order to work. Source = dependent, target = dependency. Not for where something runs (HostedOn) or monitoring (Monitors).

edge_types.name: HostedOn
edge_types.description: A guest or service RUNS ON a host, or a service runs inside a guest. Source = the hosted thing, target = where it runs. Extract one fact for EVERY guest or service whose host is stated.

edge_types.name: MigratedTo
edge_types.description: A guest or service was MOVED from one host or guest to another at a specific time. Source = the moved thing, target = the NEW location. Set the event date as the fact's valid time.

edge_types.name: Monitors
edge_types.description: The source (a monitoring service or a Workflow) watches, checks or alerts on the target (Host, Guest, Service or Network).

edge_types.name: Exposes
edge_types.description: A service is reachable through a Network, domain name, VLAN or public hostname. Source = the service, target = the network or hostname.

edge_types.name: BacksUpTo
edge_types.description: A host or guest is backed up to a Storage target. Source = what is backed up, target = the storage.

edge_types.name: CausedBy
edge_types.description: An Incident was caused by the target (a Service, Host, Guest, Decision, change or event). Only when the text states or implies the cause.

edge_types.name: ResolvedBy
edge_types.description: An Incident was resolved by the target (a Decision, action, fix or change). Source = the Incident, target = the fix.

edge_types.name: LocatedAt
edge_types.description: An entity is situated at or within a location

edge_types.name: Owns
edge_types.description: An ownership or possession relationship between an entity and an object

edge_types.name: MentionedIn
edge_types.description: An entity is referenced or described within a source document or message

instructions: Infrastructure and IT operations notes. Classify every entity with the MOST SPECIFIC infrastructure type: applications = Service, LXC/VM/container = Guest, Proxmox nodes = Host, domains/hostnames/VLANs = Network, storage pools/shares = Storage. Use Organization, Location, Object or Topic only for things that are not infrastructure. Extract HostedOn for every guest or service with a stated host, MigratedTo for moves (with the date), Monitors for monitoring relations and Exposes for services reachable through a domain or hostname. Use only the listed relation types.
